background: DNB is Norway's largest bank, part-owned by the Norwegian state, funded by Norwegian deposits and covered bonds and lending to Norwegian households and companies, with a large shipping and energy book.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the bank, AA on average with the weakest at AA-, both on a stable outlook, the last move being a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 27 Sep 2023. Capital is strong, with CET1 of 17.4% and leverage of 6.3% above the EU and Nordic peer median, though CET1 has fallen 2.0 points since 31 Dec 2024. Liquidity is the weak side, with LCR of 136% and NSFR of 116% both in the bottom quarter (figures to 30 Sep 2026).
